text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: KMS decrypt errors (key-not-found / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) — alerting eng-oncall. PagerDuty incident: PD-4827. Root: high KMS error rate while serving live traffic.

pagerduty: Pager Duty notification sent to eng-oncall. escalation: primary -> sec -> oncall-manager.

alex: acked. I’m on it — looking at logs and recent key ops.

amelia: seeing spike in 5xx for generation endpoints, ~12% error rate in last 3m. Graphs: token-svc and session-proxy showing decrypt errors. Customers hitting timeouts.

matt: logs (redacted):
```
ERROR decryption failed: google.kms.v1.KmsError: NOT_FOUND: Key version "projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/rw/cryptoKeys/serve-key/cryptoKeyVersions/7" not found
ERROR retryable error: ResourceExhausted: Quota exceeded for CryptoKeyVersions.Lookup
```

kevin: also seeing bursts of `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` from the KMS control plane for the us-west1 region — likely throttling due to recent rotation job.

priya: did we rotate keys in the last 30m? I can see a rotation job kick at 1719890900 from key-rotation-runner. It started rewrapping active key versions.

alex: confirmed: automated rotation started 8m before the first alerts. It looks like rotation attempted to promote a new key version while traffic was high; some servers tried to decrypt with the new version before it was fully provisioned -> NOT_FOUND.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook: KMS transient failure playbook. Steps: 1) Pause rotation job 2) Failover to previous key version 3) Add client-side retry/backoff 4) Open cloud support case if quota issues persist.

amelia: immediate mitigation idea: stop the rotation job and rollback consumers to previous key version. Can we push a hotfix to pin decrypt key version at runtime?

matt: we have a toggle in config: `SERVE_KEY_VERSION` that the services read at startup — but many pods cache the key version in memory. We'll need to push a rolling restart or a config reload to enforce the old version.

alex: doing the quick steps now: 1) pausing rotation job (key-rotation-runner) -> `kubectl scale deployment/key-rotation-runner --replicas=0` 2) set `SERVE_KEY_VERSION=v6` in config map for token-svc and session-proxy -> rolling restart 3) enable aggressive retries in the KMS client (exponential backoff).

kevin: I’ve paused the rotation job. Confirmed replicas=0.

priya: changing config and triggering rolling restarts for token-svc and session-proxy. Watch logs for decrypt success.

matt: applied `SERVE_KEY_VERSION=v6` to token-svc; initiating restart. Restart batch 1/4.

amelia: after first restart, decrypt errors drop to 3% for that host. Overall cluster still ~7% — continuing restarts.

alex: temporarily increasing KMS client retry window and jitter to reduce pressure: set max attempts=6, base delay=200ms.

pagerduty: Incident PD-4827 acknowledged by alex. Escalation stopped.

matt: restarted all instances of token-svc and session-proxy in us-west1. Decrypt errors now down to ~0.7% and still falling. Throughput normalizing.

kevin: contacted cloud KMS support (case C-55912) — they reported a transient throttling event in the regional control plane correlated with key promotion activity. They recommended spreading rotations or using staged rollout.

priya: customer impact: intermittent 5xx for some API calls between 1719891000-1719892500. We should prepare a customer-facing blurb and incident severity.

alex: setting Sev-2. Draft blurb for status.redwood.ai: "We identified increased error rates for API calls caused by key rotation and KMS throttling; mitigation applied and service recovering. We are investigating root cause and next steps." Thoughts?

amelia: include guidance: no API keys or data compromised; this is availability-only. Note time window and affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat.

matt: after conversation with KMS, we should: 1) change rotation to staged rollout across regions and a small concurrency cap 2) add pre-warm step to ensure key version availability 3) add metrics on key-version lookup latency and NOT_FOUND counts 4) add a circuit-breaker to prevent mass promotion during high traffic windows.

kevin: created follow-up ticket: INF-1298 (Change rotation to staged rollout + add pre-warm). Assigning to infra/crypto.

priya: handoff: I need to take the next shift for post-incident clean up and communications. Alex — anything else for me?

alex: thanks — primary actions complete. Please: 1) keep PD incident open until cloud confirms full stabilization, 2) update status page with timeline + customer impact, 3) coordinate postmortem.

priya: ack. I’ll open the incident doc and start timeline. Linking PD: PD-4827, support case: C-55912.

sre-runbook-bot: Reminder: add blameless postmortem, link logs, and export KMS audit entries for timeframe 1719890800-1719894000.

amelia: minor note: some services fell back to cached keys and served traffic fine — that's why errors were not total outage. We should capture which services do client-side caching properly.

matt: also found a small bug in rotation-runner: it didn't wait for `cryptoKeyVersion` to reach `READY` before marking as active. Adding pre-warm check in INF-1298.

kevin: monitoring: set an alert threshold for `kms.lookup_not_found_count > 5/min` and `kms.resource_exhausted > 1/min` so we get earlier paging.

alex: signed off for now — handing to priya for post-incident work. Great job everyone. :thumbsup:

priya: taking over. Will post updates in incident doc and follow up with infra/crypto for INF-1298. On-call outgoing handoff to priya at 1719893000.

pagerduty: PD-4827 status: Mitigated; oncall acknowledging handoff.

incident-bot: Closing thread? Leave open until postmortem created.

priya: leaving a final ephemeral note for customers: "Update: root cause identified as an aggressive key rotation promoting key versions during high traffic and triggering KMS throttling. Mitigations applied; full recovery in progress. We will follow up with a detailed postmortem and changes to rotation process."

alex: quick TODOs (recording here):
- INF-1298 (rotation staged rollout + pre-warm) -> infra/crypto
- Add `SERVE_KEY_VERSION` hot-reload or safer promotion path -> platform
- Add KMS throttling alerts and quota dashboards -> observability
- Update runbook with step to pause rotation under high error rates -> runbooks

priya: creating the incident doc now and will schedule a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow.

amelia: closing note: no customer data leaked. All changes were availability-related only.

alex: thanks team. Closing oncall thread but keeping PD/ticket links in the incident doc.
